FOREWORD This Indian Standard (Second Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Metal Containers Sectional Committee had been approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council. This standard was first published in 1982 and subsequently revised in 1988. With the promulgation of the Standards of Weights and Measures (Packaged Commodities) Third Amendment Rules, 1994, the edible oils, Ghee, Vanaspati and butter oils may be packed by mass or volume basis, it had become necessary to make suitable provisions in the standard. The rule also states that in case packing has been done on mass basis declaration of volume within brackets and if it is done on volume basis declaration of mass within brackets is to be done. The standard and 200 g/ml edible oils by of the product has been revised to cover tins for packing 10 kg/litre, 5 kg/litre, 2 kg/litre, 1 kg/litre, 500 g/ml of Ghee, Vanaspati and all other edible oils including bakery shortenings or nitrogen dispersed making provisions for keeping different heights to suit the specific gravity and sullage requirements to be packed into it.

For the purpose of deciding whether a,particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result ofa test, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)`. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of specified value in this standard.

IS 10339 : 2000

Indian Standard GHEE, VANASPATI, EDIBLE OIL TINS UP TO 10 kg/litre CAPACITY - SPECIFICATION ( Second Revision )
1 SCOPE This standard specifies the requirements of lO~kg/litre square tins; 5 kg/litre, 2 kg/litre, 1 kg/litre, 500 g/ml and 200 g/ml round and square tins used for packing of Ghee, Vanaspati and edible oils including nitrogen dispersed edible oils (bakery shortenings). 2 REFERENCES The following Indian Standards contain provisions which through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. At the time of publication, the editions indicated were valid. All standards are subject to revision and parties to agreements based on this standard are ~encouraged to investigate the possibility of applying the most recent editions of the standards indicated-below. IS No. 280 : 1978 998 (Part 1) : 1983 Title Mil~d steel wire for -general engineering purposes (third revision) Methods of chemical analysis of solders (soft and rosin cored): Part 1 Determination of tin antimony (first revision) Method of determination of mass of tin coating on tinplate (third revision) Glossary of terms relating to metal containers (third revision) Single cold-reduced tinplate and single cold-reduced blackplateElectrolytic and hot-dipped tinplate sheet and blackplate sheet (third revision) Methods of test for metal containers Methods for sampling of metal containers Double cold-reduced electrolytic tinplate sheet 4 REQUIREMENTS 4.1 Shape and Dimensions 4.1.1 Round and Square Tins up to 5 kg/litre Round tins up to 5 kg/litre capacity for Ghee, Vanaspati and edible oils shall be of the shape and dimensions as given in Table 1 read with Fig. 1. The dimensions of 5 kg/litre and 2 kg/litre round tins for nitrogen dispersed Vanaspati shall be as given in Table 2 read with Fig. 1. The shape and dimensions for 5 kg/litre and 2 kg/litre square tins for edible oils and bakery shortenings shall be as given in Table 3. 4.1.2 10 kg/litre Square Tins The 10 kg/litre square tins shall be manufactured to the dimensions given in Fig. 2. Depending upon the product to be filled in the tins, namely, Ghee, Vanaspati, edible oils, bakery shortenings, etc, the height of the tin may be varied to contain 10 kg/litre of the product, and shall be as specified by the purchaser. 4.2 Material 4.2.1 Body and Ends 4.2.1.1 For 5 kg/litre, 2 kg/litre, 1 ~kg/litre, 500 g/ml and 200 g/ml, the body and ends of the tins shall be made from tin plate of the nominal thickness as given in Tables 1, 2 and 3. Standard grade single coldreduced electrolytic tin plate conforming to IS 1993 or standard grade double cold-reduced electrolytic tin plate conforming to IS 13954 shall be used for the body and ends of tins. 4.2.1.2 For 10 kg/litre square tins, standard grade single cold-reduced electrolytic tinplate of nominal thickness 0.28 mm conforming to IS 1993 or standard grade double cold-reduced electrolytic tinplate of nominal thickness 0.21 mm conforming to IS 13954 shall he used for the body, ends and capseals on lids of tins. 4.2.2 Lid Components 4.2.2.1 For lid components of tins up to 5 kg/litre capacity, standard grade single reduced electrolytic tinplate of nominal thickness 0.19 mm conforming to IS 1993 or standard grade double cold-reduced electrolytic tinplate of nominal thickness 0.15 mm 1

4.2.4 Undertagger When the undertagger is required, it shall be made of aluminium foil. The minimum thickness of aluminium foil shall be 0.050 mm for tins up to 1 kg&e capacity and 0.064 mm for tins above 1 kg/litre capacity, of minimum thickness 0.064 mm. Alternate material may be used, if agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 4.2.5 Solder The solder used shall have minimum tin content of 2 percent for machine soldering and 40 percent for hand soldering. The antimony content of the solder shall not exceed 6 percent of the tin content. The tin 3

standard grade single reduced electrolytic tinplate of nominal thickness 0.28 mm conforming to IS 1993 or standard grade double cold-reduced electrolytic tinplate of nominal thickness 0.2 1 mm conforming to IS 13954 shall be used. 4.2.3 The tin coating thickness shall be of grade E 2.812.8. The tin coating shall be checked by the method given in IS 1327 or any other established instrumental or chemical method. The tins for Ghee shall be given a suitable lacquer coating on the inside.

diameter. If agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier, phosphated or painted iron wire may also be used. 4.3 Manufacture 4.3.1 For tins up to 5 kg/litre capacity, the body shall be a single piece construction, soldered or welded as shown in Fig. 3A and 3B. For 10 kg/litre tins, the body may be a single or two piece construction, soldered or welded as shown in Fig. 3A and 3B. The welded seam shall be coated with a suitable lacquer

on the inside and outside and the soldered seam shall be coated with a suitable sidestripe lacquer on the outside only. 4.3.1.1 For 10 kg/litre tins, all the four sides and the top and bottom end panels shall be stiffened by embossing or panelling. The embossing designs shown in Fig. 2 are illustrative and may be changed at the option of the manufacturer. Bottom end panelling shall be the same as for the top end. 4.3.2 The top and bottom ends shall be made of one

piece and joined to the body by either a single or double seam as shown in Fig. 4A and 4B. Single seam shall be fully soldered whereas double seam shall be lined with a non-toxic compound or fully soldered. 4.3.3 Closures The recommended types of closures for each size of tins are as given in Table 4 read with Fig. 5. For 10 kg/litre tins, the aperture edge shall be located at least 14 mm away from the inside edge of the top seam.

4.3.4 Handle

A wire handle of the design and dimensions as shown in Fig. 6 shall be provided on the top centre of the 10 kg/litre and 5 kg/litre tins. Handle shall be firmly secured to the top by soldering, spot welding or projection welding. The handle may be fixed parallel to the sides as shown in Fig. 6 or in the diagonal position as required by~the purchaser. Other suitable types, shape and sizes of handle may also be used, if agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 4.3.5 Supply Condition The tins shall be supplied in new and~clean conditions from inside and outside. They shall be free from all traces of rust and foreign materials. 4.3.6 Internal Finish For Vanaspati and edible oils, the tins shall be plain inside. For Ghee, the tins and closure components shall be given a suitable lacquer coating inside. The welded side seam shall be coated internally with a suitable side stripe lacquer to prevent it from rusting. 4.3.7 Outside Finish The outside surface of the body of~tins may be given a protective or decorative coating or both, if required by the purchaser. 5 TESTING 5.1 Air Pressure Test 5.1.1 The tins up to 5 kg/litre capacity without its loose closure components shall be subjected to an air pressure of 15 kPa (0.15 kgf/cm*), minimum for 15 seconds. The tin shall show no sign of leakage when 6
4A Single 48 Double

FIG. 4 END SEAMS immersed in water. The test shall be carried out as prescribed in 3 of IS 247 1. 5.1.2 Each 10 kg/litre square tin shall be subjected to an air pressure of 8 kPa (0.08 kgf/cm*), minimum for 15 seconds. The tin shall show no sign of leakage when immersed in water. The test shall be carried out as prescribed in 3 of IS 2471. 5.2 Hydraulic Pressure Test (for 10 kg/We Square Tin Only) The~representative samples of 10 kg/litre square tins shall be subjected to hydraulic pressure test of 30 kPa (0.30 kgf/cm*) for a period of not less than 3 minutes and shall show no sign of leakage. The test shall be carried out as prescribed in 4 of IS 247 1. 5.3 Handle Pull Test The representative samples of tins shail be subjected
